$comment: The receipt contract, in one machine-readable place. The validator (scripts/receipt-gate.mjs) derives its rules from here, and `receipt-gate.mjs --check` walks every landing point below — so bumping the Schema version, renaming a field, or changing the Conclusion vocabulary cannot land in one document and silently miss the others. Landing-point tokens use the {schema} placeholder, expanded from the `schema` field at check time; the checker additionally scans every landing point for any spec-executor-receipt/v<N> other than the current one, so a half-finished version bump fails instead of passing. Historical records are deliberately NOT landing points: docs/evals/results/**, docs/evals/tasks/**, closed draft proposals, and ADRs describe what was true at the time and must never be rewritten to match today's contract.
heading: SPEC EXECUTION RECEIPT
$conclusionSemantics: One single token on the first line; a justification sentence may follow on the next line. `completed` is the only outcome archive gate 1 admits. Partial work is reported as `blocked` (with the remainder listed) — never as a two-word token, which gate 3 rejects by design.
$fieldsComment: The exhaustive set of lines that start a new field. The parser needs it because an Acceptance criteria entry is shaped exactly like a field (`- AC1: …`): without this list the criteria block ended at the first entry and gate 4 graded the wrong text — silently, since every later field still parsed. A receipt field that is missing here is read as a continuation of the previous field, so this list and the launch prompt in skills/engineering/spec-executor/SKILL.md must agree.

gates.label: 工作树终态无意外漂移

$requiredFields: Every field the receipt template must carry, in order. The first entry is the pin the validator checks as a structural precondition; the rest are the evidence the six gates read. Consumers use this list instead of hardcoding their own copy, so a field rename lands in one place.

landingPoints.$comment: Delivery documents are the project's process artifacts, not the contract. Checked while present so they cannot drift, skipped once archived — a validator that breaks because a design document was filed elsewhere is coupling, not rigour.
